title: The Swarm on Elastic
about: the best of Kibana and Grafana, for the agentic swarm at Web Summit

scenes.title: Everything the swarm does lands on one stack
scenes.headline: Every run, every agent, every model call. One stack.
lines: Three public sites, built by about 200 agents for 6 people, since 28 October.
Every unit of work signs its own result: the A4 swarm, A3 agents, A2 loops, A1 model calls, A0 compute.

lines.text: It all goes to Elastic, from wherever it runs: Claude Code, GitHub Actions, OpenRouter.

scenes.footnote: Read from the deployment at 07:46 UTC, 12 November 2026 (_cat/indices; ES|QL on *-commits, swarm-flows, traces-generic.otel-default).
scenes.say: Open with the scale. Everything you'll see is live data: three public repositories, the agents' own run records, and OpenRouter's traces of every model call. Nothing was typed in by hand.
scenes.lead: The scale, from the deployment itself.

scenes.title: The swarm's runs, drawn the stage's way
scenes.lead: The swarm's stage, rebuilt inside Kibana from swarm-flows.

callouts.label: One storm run: about 93 units in 50 seconds, each bar one unit with its own key.
callouts.point: Every bar is a unit of work that started, ran and signed its result: A3 agent at the top, A1 model calls and A0 compute below.

callouts.label: The whole evening: the runs climb the ladder, A0 up to A4.
callouts.point: As the night went on, the runs moved up the altitudes: compute first, then model calls, then loops and agents.

callouts.label: 369 model calls and 319 compute steps under 76 loops and 8 agents.
callouts.point: The ladder: most work is cheap, small and low down. That is the point of the altitudes.

callouts.label: 93% of the units ran in GitHub Actions (R8), not in a chat session.
callouts.point: The same records come from any environment: Claude Code cloud (R1) and GitHub Actions (R8) here.

scenes.say: This is the swarm's own stage, rebuilt in Kibana with Vega-Lite: the same altitude lanes and the same colours, straight from the swarm-flows index. Hover any bar in the live view for its model, cost and outcome. Red edges are invalid answers that were retried.
scenes.source: swarm-flows (architect.1's flow.mjs, swarm.1 in GitHub Actions); dashboard 11, admin/tools/elastic-kibana.mjs

scenes.title: Every unit signs, and we can see who held too much
scenes.lead: The operating model's rules, as data.

callouts.label: Every unit of every run, by the time its key was born.
callouts.point: Each unit gets its own key when it starts and signs when it ends.

callouts.label: Each run as a tree: depth, altitude and role.
callouts.point: An agent starts loops; loops start model calls and compute. The tree is in the data.

callouts.label: One key per unit, born to signed: 130 of 132 verified.
callouts.point: The two without a signature are agents, which sign with their session key.

callouts.label: Loops and compute held 20 to 22 capabilities they did not need.
callouts.point: Mixing altitudes: the low units inherited the agent's reach. This is the finding the policy now watches (R12).

callouts.label: 38% of the first answers were invalid and retried.
callouts.point: Cheap open-weight calls fail more often, and the retries are visible and cheap.

scenes.say: Dinis and Angelo's model: the same shape at every size, an objective, a mandate, a grant, a key and a signed result. Here it is as data. The keys panel proves each unit signed; the mixing panel shows the one thing to fix, units that held far more than they needed.
scenes.source: fringe-altitudes (architect.1's data/altitude-runs.json, from signed sources only); dashboard 7

scenes.title: One query, the whole ladder
scenes.lead: Type it live: one ES|QL query answers the altitude question.
scenes.say: Switch to Discover and type this live. One ES|QL query over the runs gives units, cost, average duration and invalid answers per altitude. No dashboard needed: the question is the query.
scenes.source: FROM swarm-flows | WHERE phase == "end" | STATS units, usd, avg_ms, invalid BY altitude

scenes.title: Every model call, from the provider's side
scenes.lead: OpenRouter sends a trace of every call straight to Elastic.

callouts.label: OpenRouter spread the calls across many providers.
callouts.point: One request, many possible providers: the trace says which one answered.

callouts.panel: Time to first token by model
callouts.label: Open-weight models answer in about 130 to 200 ms; frontier in about 1.9 s.
callouts.point: Speed and cost per model, measured, not quoted.

callouts.label: Calls cut at the token limit show up at once.
callouts.point: We caught our own max_tokens set too low within minutes.

callouts.panel: Open-weight and frontier side by side
callouts.label: Per model and provider: calls, cost, tokens, latency.
callouts.point: The table you take to a procurement conversation.

scenes.say: We switched on OpenRouter's Broadcast: every model call any agent makes arrives as an OpenTelemetry trace, with model, provider, tokens, cost and time to first token. Prompts are kept in the traces by Dinis's decision, and shown on no panel.

scenes.title: Three sites, 11,000 commits, one view

callouts.label: Every commit on the three sites, hour by hour since 28 October.
callouts.point: Read from the public repositories; each commit attributed to its agent from its Agent: trailer.

callouts.label: The busiest agents across all three sites.
callouts.point: About 200 agents; under 1% of commits stay unattributed.

callouts.label: Who works where: each person's agents, by site.
callouts.point: One person, several sites, many agents: the swarm's shape.

scenes.say: The swarm's whole output since 28 October: every commit on the three public sites, attributed to the agent that made it. This is the view a manager asks for: who did what, where, and when.

scenes.title: The engine finds the moment the pace changed
scenes.say: One more ES|QL query, live: commits per hour across the three sites, and CHANGE_POINT finds where the pace changed, a trend change on 10 November at 17:00 UTC, with a p-value of about 10⁻⁷. Nobody told it where to look.
scenes.source: FROM *-commits | STATS commits = COUNT(*) BY bucket = BUCKET(t, 1 hour) | CHANGE_POINT commits ON bucket

scenes.title: Many agents write to Elastic; one steward watches
scenes.lead: Every submission, by every agent, audited.

callouts.label: Every submission, push or feed, by agent.
callouts.point: Agents write to their own indices; the owner is recorded in the index itself.

scenes.say: Elastic isn't one agent's tool: any agent can push to its own index or commit a feed. Privacy checks hold back anything that looks like an email, a phone or a key; this dashboard shows every submission and anything held.

scenes.title: How it's built
scenes.headline: All of it is code, and all of it refreshes every hour.
lines: Ingest tools read the public repositories and the agents' signed records; every document carries its source, read time and signer.
Privacy checks run on every document: contact details, private people and keys are held back before they leave.
Dashboards are generated from one script; any agent can add its own from a spec in its own folder.

lines.text: Same data, many views: Kibana, Discover, Vega, Grafana, and the swarm's own stage.
